body.statement: Using the finite-risk saddle handle, characterize the dosage in \(\mathcal D_L\) minimizing the worst-case unconditional risk of the specified spectral-threshold OLS estimator over \(\|\beta\|_2\le B\) and the admissible conditional-noise class. Determine an explicit finite-\(n\) frontier separating regimes in which \(d^\star\) is minimax from regimes in which a nonuniform independent dosage has strictly smaller worst-case risk.
body.justification: Population \(A\)-optimality does not settle the discontinuous finite-sample risk created by missing patterns and fallback bias.
body.gap: ShyamalZhangUhler2025 proves only near-optimal bounds, and DerezinskiWarmuth2017 obtains exact inverse-Gram identities under a different dependent sampling law.
body.consumer: The frontier would tell small interaction screens whether the asymptotically optimal uniform dosage is also the correct finite-budget design.

obligation.what_is_open: An explicit finite-\(n\) comparison over \(d\in\mathcal D_L\) requires a dosage-indexed spectral event, estimator, bad-event probability, and unconditional risk, followed by solution of the resulting nonconvex finite-support optimization.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen objects \(G_n(\varepsilon)\), \(\widehat\beta_\varepsilon\), and \(R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon)\) are defined only using \(\Sigma_k(d^\star)\) and expectation under \(P_{d^\star}\). Thus the frozen core contains no well-typed objective map whose argument is a competing dosage \(d\), so no minimizer or frontier over \(\mathcal D_L\) can be proved without first adding that construction and specifying its threshold convention.
obligation.attempted: I substituted the exact conditional-risk decomposition, maximized its two nonnegative terms over the coefficient ball and variance interval, and reduced the assignment expectation to a finite Boolean-support sum. This closes the coefficient/noise saddle at \(d^\star\), but permutation symmetry does not compare different product dosages, and extending the estimator by silently replacing \(d^\star\) with \(d\) would change the frozen construction and the question's formal scope.
obligation.partial_result:
At the single dosage \(d^\star\) for which the frozen estimator and risk are defined, the proved decomposition gives the computable worst-case value
\[
 \sup_{\substack{\|\beta\|_2\le B,\ 
 \sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\\
 \text{admissible conditional-noise laws}}}
 R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon)
 =\sigma_{\max}^2\mathbb E_{d^\star}\!\left[
 \mathbf 1_{G_n(\varepsilon)}\operatorname{tr}\{(F^{\mathsf T}F)^{-1}\}\right]
 +B^2b_{n,\varepsilon}.
\]
The equality follows because the two terms depend on \(\sigma^2\) and \(\|\beta\|_2^2\), respectively, with nonnegative coefficients, and admissible centered homoskedastic noise laws exist at every allowed variance. This settles the worst-case coefficient/noise optimization at \(d^\star\), but it does not define or compare the corresponding quantity at \(d\ne d^\star\).
